name: Procyanidin oral (melasma)

lead: Oral procyanidin, a plant polyphenol, is taken together with vitamins A, C and E to fade melasma, the brownish facial patches that make skin tone look uneven. The payoff people want is a more uniform complexion on the cheeks and face, worked on from the inside rather than with a cream.

The idea is that antioxidant activity reduces the pigment behind the patches. An 8-week placebo-controlled trial in 56 women with epidermal melasma reported improvement on the cheeks. That is the one trial in the sources reviewed.

paras: It is taken as a daily supplement over several weeks, the length of the reported trial, and is usually thought of as a complement to sun protection and topical melasma care. Users look for gradual fading of patches rather than a quick change.

The trial summary describes the regimen as safe and well tolerated. Long-term safety data were not found. Melasma patches commonly darken again with sun exposure, so people usually pair any approach with sunscreen.

chain: Antioxidant pill with vitamins A, C, E
angle.text: Users take oral procyanidin with vitamins A, C and E to fade melasma patches and even out facial skin tone from the inside. The antioxidant combination is meant to reduce pigment in the skin, and an 8-week placebo-controlled trial in 56 women reported improvement on the cheeks.

lead: Oral procyanidin combined with vitamins A, C and E is an antioxidant supplement regimen tested for melasma, a condition of brown or gray-brown facial patches. People interested in it want a pill that evens out facial pigmentation from the inside, as a complement to sunscreen and topical lighteners, for a clearer and more uniform complexion.

The main published study is an 8-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial by Handog and colleagues in Manila, published in 2009 in the International Journal of Dermatology. It enrolled 60 women with bilateral epidermal melasma (Fitzpatrick skin types III to V), and 56 finished.[1] Instrument readings showed reduced pigmentation in both cheek regions and MASI scores improved, and the regimen was described as safe and well tolerated with minimal adverse events.[1] Wikipedia lists it among oral options for melasma.[2]

Dermatology reviews describe melasma as a chronic, recurrence-prone condition where no single treatment is universally effective and combinations often perform best.[3] The oral procyanidin regimen has no independent replication located here.
infobox: Procyanidin with vitamins A, C and E [1]

paras: Oral agents for melasma named by Wikipedia include tranexamic acid, procyanidin with vitamins A, C and E, and, from a systematic review, Polypodium leucotomos extract, beta-carotenoids and melatonin, which the review found effective with few and mild adverse events [2]. Standard care generally centers on topicals, sun avoidance and broad-spectrum sunscreen [2].

Standard care for melasma generally centers on topicals, sun avoidance and broad-spectrum sunscreen.[2] Looksmax.org threads on skin lightening and melasma compile treatment lists drawn from review tables, with oral agents such as Polypodium leucotomos appearing among them.[4]

The Handog 2009 trial randomized 60 adult women with bilateral epidermal melasma to oral procyanidin with vitamins A, C and E or placebo, taken twice daily with meals for 8 weeks; 56 completed. Mexameter pigmentation readings fell significantly in the left and right malar regions, MASI scores improved in both, and treatment was safe and well tolerated with minimal adverse events.[1] Wikipedia summarizes it as showing significant improvement in the malar regions.[2]

A 2022 systematic review of melasma treatments reports that tranexamic acid and Polypodium leucotomos had promising results, that recurrence is high across treatments, and that combination therapy performed best.[3]

Procyanidins are polyphenols found in plants such as French maritime pine bark, and are described as having antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; the trial paper does not itself establish how the regimen reduces pigment.[1]

lore.intro: Oral options for melasma and skin lightening are discussed on looksmax.org in lists compiled from review articles, mainly alongside topical agents.[4]
